claims.text: Applying a 20–30 nm ALD-deposited alumina coating to zirconium-alloy cladding will significantly reduce its high-temperature oxidation rate relative to uncoated cladding.
The ultrathin alumina coating will preserve the cladding’s in-service mechanical properties.
The ultrathin alumina coating will preserve the cladding’s in-service thermal properties.
The proposed intervention is deposition of a conformal 20–30 nm Al2O3 coating by atomic layer deposition.
The proposed coating is expected to function in oxidizing steam environments at temperatures up to approximately 1150°C.
Steam exposure near 1150°C is representative of severe reactor-accident conditions.
ALD will produce a pinhole-free alumina layer on the zirconium-alloy cladding.
The ALD-produced alumina layer will be amorphous.
The alumina layer will uniformly cover the cladding surface.
The dense alumina layer will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
Limiting oxygen ingress will reduce oxidation of the underlying zirconium alloy.
The nanometric coating thickness will minimize adverse effects from thermal-expansion mismatch.
Minimizing thermal-expansion mismatch will preserve cladding integrity.
The ALD-coated cladding will have a lower oxidation rate than cladding with conventional thicker coatings.
Adhesion and durability under rapid or repeated thermal cycling may limit the coating’s performance.
Long-term adhesion and interface stability under repeated thermal cycles and severe-accident conditions remain uncertain.
